_readme: Numbers the scripts read, so a planning decision never depends on a constant retyped into prose. Every value here was measured; docs/MEASUREMENTS.md says where. Edit this file to calibrate a different machine or a different application, and re-measure with scripts/fleet-load.mjs and scripts/fleet-retro.mjs rather than guessing. NOTE: fleet.sh reads the most recently written copy it can find - the one beside itself, or any installed version under ~/.claude/plugins/cache. Editing a checkout while an install is newer means the install wins, so edit the copy you actually run, or reinstall after editing.

_provenance.repo_tasks_per_worker: M16 - measured throughput 2.87 and 4.25 tasks per hour per worker on repo-heavy runs
_provenance.repo_worker_ceiling: M21 - a session with no pane is ~330 MB, so the ceiling is attention rather than memory
_provenance.pane_workers_default: M15 - seven panes carried 104 minutes of driving in a 153 minute run
_provenance.frame_gate_min_fps: M01, M02 - below 60 the pane is blind and everything it returns is fiction
_provenance.budget_multiplier: PULL.md - a worker past twice its budget hands the remainder back
_provenance.fanout_default: M13 - a subagent spends ~45k tokens before it does anything, so a part must be worth a slice of work. Read by a planner rather than by a script: LANES.md applies it.
_provenance.max_run_minutes: A ceiling, not a measurement: comparable tools have documented runs that looped for days and cost thousands. A run past this is a decision to continue, not a default.
_provenance.hook_claim_window_minutes: M03 - the workers that died had claimed within the minute; past ten a quiet claim is long work, and the planner's sweep owns it
_provenance.quiet_interval_seconds: Read by a planner when it arms the watch loop in fleet-wait.md, not by any script here.
_provenance.delegate_past_tasks: M30 - a repo worker's context grows 20-30 k per task worked inline and four workers were compacted near their thirtieth; the first three buy the worktree and the traps, after that fleet.sh next says DELEGATE
_provenance.pane_workers_display_ceiling: Read by a planner, not by a script: BROWSER.md is where the display ceiling is applied.
_provenance.min_path_segments: A path is got wrong at its end - an empty variable, a dirname too many - which turns it into its own parent. Depth is therefore the margin for error, counted in mistakes: C:/wtmerge is one slip from the drive root, <project>/.claude/worktrees/wtA is seven. Four is the floor fleet.sh will delete below. Not a measurement: a chosen floor.
